project.name: Damn Vulnerable RESTaurant
project.description: An intentionally vulnerable FastAPI-based REST API designed for security training — developers fix vulnerabilities interactively, ethical hackers exploit them as CTF challenges, security engineers test automated tools.

nodes.name: exceptions.py
nodes.summary: Defines the UserAlreadyExistsException custom exception raised when a duplicate user registration is attempted.

nodes.name: jwt_auth.py
nodes.summary: Provides the get_current_user FastAPI dependency that decodes a JWT bearer token and returns the authenticated user from the database.

nodes.name: get_current_user
nodes.summary: FastAPI dependency that validates the JWT bearer token, extracts the username payload, and fetches the corresponding User record from the database.

nodes.name: utils.py
nodes.summary: Core authentication utility module providing password hashing, user lookup, user creation, JWT token generation, and a stub SMS code sender.

nodes.name: create_user

nodes.name: authenticate_user

nodes.name: create_access_token
nodes.summary: Encodes a JWT access token with an optional expiry delta using the configured secret key and algorithm.

nodes.name: update_user_password
nodes.summary: Fetches a user by username, hashes the new password, and persists the change to the database.

nodes.name: update_user

nodes.name: get_user_by_username
nodes.summary: Queries the database for a User record by username, returning None if not found.

nodes.name: service.py

nodes.name: get_debug_info_service.py
nodes.summary: Collects and returns sensitive server-side information (OS details, working directory, file listing, disk, and memory usage) for the debug endpoint, intentionally exposing system data.

nodes.name: get_debug_info_service
nodes.summary: Gathers platform metadata, current working directory listing, disk usage, and virtual memory stats into a response dict representing an intentional information disclosure vulnerability.

nodes.name: service.py
nodes.summary: Provides a simple healthcheck endpoint that returns HTTP 200 to confirm the API is running.

nodes.name: MenuItem

nodes.name: update_menu_item

nodes.name: delete_menu_item

nodes.name: get_token

nodes.name: register_user

nodes.name: reset_password_new_password_service.py

nodes.name: update_profile_service.py

nodes.name: update_profile
nodes.summary: Replaces all fields on the current user's profile with the provided UserUpdate payload and commits the changes via SQLAlchemy.

nodes.name: __init__.py

nodes.name: roles_based_auth_checker.py

nodes.name: test_roles_based_auth_checker.py

nodes.name: test_referral_service.py

nodes.name: test_get_token_returns_token_with_200

nodes.name: test_register_by_authenticated_user_returns_400

nodes.languageNotes: Uses SQLAlchemy ORM with explicit rollback on partial failures when inserting order items.

nodes.name: create_order
nodes.summary: FastAPI endpoint handler that validates coupon and menu items, creates an Order record with its associated OrderItems, and applies discount logic with transactional rollback on errors.

nodes.name: get_order_service.py
nodes.summary: Provides the get_order endpoint handler that retrieves a single order by ID with role-based authentication, returning 404 if the order is not found.

nodes.name: get_order

nodes.name: get_order_status.py
nodes.summary: Implements order status retrieval by calling an external delivery service and updating order status in the database via a raw SQL query, exposing an intentional SQL injection vulnerability.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses db.execute(text(...)) with string interpolation to build the SQL UPDATE — this is a deliberate SQL injection vulnerability for the CTF training context.

nodes.name: OrderStatusResponse
nodes.summary: Pydantic response model containing the order status string and order ID returned by the get_order_status endpoint.

nodes.name: get_order_status
nodes.summary: FastAPI handler that fetches the delivery status for an order from an external service and persists it via a raw SQL update, introducing an intentional SQL injection vulnerability.

nodes.name: get_orders_for_delivery_service.py
nodes.summary: Provides a paginated endpoint for retrieving all orders sorted by date for delivery staff, without user-based filtering to allow delivery role access.

nodes.name: get_orders
nodes.summary: FastAPI handler that returns a paginated, date-sorted list of all orders for the delivery role, without ownership filtering.

nodes.name: get_orders_service.py
nodes.summary: Implements paginated retrieval of orders scoped to the authenticated user's ID with role-based authorization.

nodes.name: get_orders
nodes.summary: FastAPI handler that queries all orders belonging to the current user with pagination, enforcing role-based access control.

nodes.name: utils.py
nodes.summary: Utility module providing fetch_order_status_from_delivery_service, which makes an HTTP GET to an external delivery service endpoint using a configurable base URL — introducing an intentional SSRF vulnerability.
nodes.languageNotes: Builds the external URL directly from user-supplied order_id against a configurable delivery service base URL, enabling SSRF.

nodes.name: fetch_order_status_from_delivery_service
nodes.summary: Makes an HTTP GET to the configured external delivery service URL using the order ID, returning the JSON response — intentionally vulnerable to SSRF.

nodes.summary: SQLAlchemy model for discount coupons with a code, percentage value, and usage constraints applied during order creation.

nodes.name: test_admin_service.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the admin service covering password reset authorization (403 for unauthorized, 200 from localhost) and disk stats access control, verifying correct role enforcement.

nodes.name: test_menu_service.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the menu service verifying that GET returns menu data, employees and chefs can create and delete menu items, and unauthenticated users receive 401 on delete.

nodes.name: level_1_unrestricted_menu_item_deletion.py
nodes.summary: CTF vulnerability test (Level 1) that exploits unrestricted menu item deletion by a customer role user, demonstrating broken object-level authorization.
nodes.languageNotes: Part of the intentional vulnerability test suite; passing this test means the vulnerability is still exploitable.

nodes.name: level_2_unrestricted_profile_update_IDOR.py
nodes.summary: CTF vulnerability test (Level 2) that exploits an IDOR flaw allowing a customer to update another user's profile by supplying a different user ID in the request.
nodes.languageNotes: Demonstrates an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) where the server does not verify the requester owns the target resource.

nodes.name: level_3_privilege_escalation.py
nodes.summary: CTF vulnerability test (Level 3) that exploits privilege escalation by allowing a customer to elevate their role to employee or chef via an unrestricted profile update endpoint.

nodes.name: level_4_server_side_request_forgery.py
nodes.summary: CTF vulnerability test (Level 4) that exploits SSRF by supplying a crafted delivery service URL in an order status request, causing the server to issue an internal HTTP request to the admin reset endpoint.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses requests_mock to simulate an external delivery service response and mocker.patch to intercept the internal admin call, fully exercising the SSRF attack chain.

nodes.name: update_menu_item_service.py

nodes.languageNotes: Uses a generator-based get_db dependency (yield pattern) so FastAPI ensures the session is always closed after each request, even on errors.

nodes.name: create_menu_item
nodes.summary: FastAPI route handler that creates a new menu item, requiring a valid authenticated user and role-based authorization check.

nodes.name: delete_menu_item

nodes.summary: Private factory that constructs the SQLAlchemy engine (with optional SQLite in-memory fallback) and returns the bound session factory.

nodes.name: get_db

nodes.name: schemas.py
nodes.summary: Defines the Pydantic response schema for the admin disk usage API, exposing a single DiskUsage model with an output field.

nodes.name: DiskUsage
nodes.summary: Pydantic response model representing disk usage output returned by the admin disk stats endpoint.

nodes.name: service.py
nodes.summary: Thin aggregation module that imports and re-exposes the admin service handlers for disk stats and chef password reset, acting as the admin services entry point.

nodes.name: get_disk_stats_service.py
nodes.summary: Implements the admin disk usage stats endpoint handler, enforcing admin-only authorization and delegating command execution to the get_disk_usage utility.

nodes.name: get_disk_usage_stats
nodes.summary: FastAPI route handler that verifies the current user has admin role and then executes the disk usage command, returning the result as a DiskUsage schema response.

nodes.name: reset_chef_password_service.py
nodes.summary: Implements the admin endpoint for resetting a chef user's password, looking up the target user and generating a new random password before persisting it.

nodes.name: get_reset_chef_password
nodes.summary: FastAPI route handler that resets a chef user's password by username: looks up the user, raises 404 if not found, generates a random password with secrets, and persists it via update_user_password.

nodes.name: utils.py
nodes.summary: Provides the get_disk_usage utility that executes an OS-level disk usage command via subprocess, passing user-supplied parameters directly — an intentional command injection vulnerability in this training application.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses subprocess.run with unsanitized user input (parameters), which is an intentional command injection vulnerability in this deliberately vulnerable API game.

nodes.name: get_disk_usage
nodes.summary: Executes a shell disk usage command using subprocess.run with user-supplied parameters, returning decoded stdout — intentionally vulnerable to OS command injection.
nodes.languageNotes: Intentional command injection: user-controlled parameters are passed directly to subprocess without sanitization.

nodes.name: reset_password_service.py
nodes.summary: Implements the password reset service for the auth API, exposing a `reset_password` endpoint handler that validates the requesting user, enforces business rules, and delegates code generation and delivery to the text code utility.

nodes.name: ResetPasswordData
nodes.summary: Pydantic-style request schema holding the `username` field required for a password reset request.

nodes.name: reset_password
nodes.summary: FastAPI route handler that looks up the user by username, raises HTTP 404 or 400 on error conditions, then calls `generate_and_send_code_to_user` to initiate the password reset flow.

nodes.name: text_code_utils.py
nodes.summary: Utility module for generating and dispatching one-time text codes to users during authentication flows such as password reset, using secrets-based random generation and a phone delivery call.

nodes.name: generate_and_send_code_to_user
nodes.summary: Generates a cryptographically random numeric code with an expiry timestamp, persists it to the database, and sends it to the user's phone number via `send_code_to_phone_number`.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `secrets.randbelow` for code generation — relevant from a security perspective as it avoids predictable `random` module values, though the overall flow may still be vulnerable to enumeration attacks.

nodes.name: rate_limiting.py
nodes.summary: Minimal module that exposes a rate limiting dependency or configuration used by API route handlers to throttle requests.

nodes.name: schemas.py
nodes.summary: Defines the Pydantic read schema for discount coupons, exposing id, discount percentage, usage status, and timestamps for API responses.

nodes.name: DiscountCouponRead
nodes.summary: Pydantic model for serializing a DiscountCoupon ORM record into an API response, including id, discount_percentage, used flag, and audit timestamps.

nodes.name: service.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI router implementing three referral endpoints: retrieving a user's referral code, applying a referral code to earn a discount coupon, and listing a user's discount coupons.

nodes.name: get_referral_code_endpoint
nodes.summary: FastAPI GET endpoint that retrieves or generates the authenticated user's referral code and returns it in a ReferralCodeResponse.

nodes.name: apply_referral_code
nodes.summary: FastAPI POST endpoint that accepts a referral code, validates the referring user, and creates a DiscountCoupon for the current user; contains an intentional IDOR vulnerability by not checking that the current user differs from the referral code owner.
nodes.languageNotes: The referral lookup uses a raw ORM query without sanitization and does not enforce that a user cannot apply their own code, making it a deliberate security training target.

nodes.name: get_discount_coupons
nodes.summary: FastAPI GET endpoint that queries and returns all discount coupons belonging to the authenticated user.

nodes.name: utils.py
nodes.summary: Provides helper functions for generating random referral codes and persisting them to the database via the User ORM model.

nodes.name: get_referral_code
nodes.summary: Generates a new random referral code if the user does not already have one, persists it via a database session, and returns the code string.

nodes.name: schemas.py
nodes.summary: Defines the UserRoleUpdate Pydantic request schema used to validate username and role fields when updating a user's role via the API.

nodes.name: UserRoleUpdate
nodes.summary: Pydantic BaseModel carrying the target username and desired role for a user role update request.

nodes.name: service.py
nodes.summary: Thin barrel module that re-exports the users service layer by importing from the update_user_role_service submodule, acting as the public surface for the users API router.

nodes.name: update_user_role_service.py
nodes.summary: Implements the PUT /users/update_role FastAPI endpoint that allows authenticated users to change another user's role; intentionally contains a broken function-level access control vulnerability — it only blocks assigning the CHEF role but does not verify the caller has staff privileges, and incorrectly returns the current user instead of the updated record.
nodes.languageNotes: Intentional BFLA (Broken Function Level Authorization) vulnerability: no role check on the caller before performing the update, only the target role is validated. Also a data-return bug: returns current_user rather than the modified db_user.

nodes.name: update_user_role
nodes.summary: Async FastAPI route handler for PUT /users/update_role that validates the requested role is not CHEF, then delegates to update_user to persist the change in the database.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml
nodes.summary: Docker Compose orchestration file that defines two services: a FastAPI web application (built from the local Dockerfile) exposed on port 8091 and a PostgreSQL 15.4 database, with the web service configured to run database migrations and reload on code changes.
nodes.languageNotes: Web service runs with privileged mode and SYS_ADMIN capability, intentional for the vulnerable-by-design training scenario.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Multi-stage Docker build that uses a Python 3.10 builder stage to export Poetry dependencies to a requirements.txt, then produces a slim runtime image that copies the app code, installs a passwordless sudo rule for /usr/bin/find as a deliberate vulnerability, and runs as a non-root user.
nodes.languageNotes: Intentionally grants passwordless sudo on /usr/bin/find (RUN echo 'ALL ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/find'), a deliberate security misconfiguration for training purposes.

nodes.name: .pre-commit-config.yaml

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README explains what Damn Vulnerable RESTaurant is and who it is for: developers learn to find and fix vulnerabilities, ethical hackers exploit them as a CTF challenge escalating from a low-privileged API user to root, and security engineers test automated SAST/DAST/IaC tools. Reading it first establishes the game's three personas and the single escalation path that the rest of the tour will trace in code.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: main.py is the runtime starting point: it creates all database tables, runs the seed script, and launches the uvicorn server. Its six imports fan out to every major subsystem (factory, config, session, models, seed, game), making it the single file that assembles the whole application. Understanding what it calls — and in what order — is the skeleton key for navigating the codebase.
tour.languageLesson: Python's `if __name__ == '__main__'` guard lets a module be both importable (for tests) and directly executable (for the server). Uvicorn is an ASGI server; FastAPI apps are ASGI-compatible, so passing the app object's import string (e.g., 'app.main:app') lets uvicorn hot-reload without re-importing the whole module.

tour.title: App Factory & Configuration
tour.description: init_app.py implements the factory pattern: it constructs the FastAPI instance, attaches CORS middleware, and mounts the central API router — separating creation from startup. config.py feeds it by reading environment variables for JWT secrets, database URLs, CORS origins, and game-mode flags. Both files are imported at depth 1 from main.py, meaning every other module inherits whatever settings are loaded here.
tour.languageLesson: The factory pattern in FastAPI (creating the app object in a dedicated function rather than at module top-level) is essential for testing: each test can call the factory to get a fresh app instance rather than reusing global state. Environment variables are typically loaded with `pydantic-settings` BaseSettings, which provides type validation and `.env` file support.

tour.title: Data Layer: Models & Session
tour.description: models.py is the most imported file in the entire graph (fanIn=11): it defines the SQLAlchemy ORM tables — User, MenuItem, Order, OrderItem, DiscountCoupon — plus the UserRole and OrderStatus enums that drive access control logic throughout the API. session.py (fanIn=10) pairs with it by providing the engine, the SessionLocal factory, and the get_db dependency generator that every route handler injects. These two files are the bedrock that every domain service sits on top of.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI's dependency injection system (`Depends`) pairs cleanly with SQLAlchemy sessions: `get_db` yields a session and closes it after the response, preventing connection leaks. The `UserRole` enum stored in the database is the same Python object checked in authorization logic, so a mismatch between the DB value and the code's enum is a common source of access-control bugs.

tour.title: Database Seed & Hardcoded Credentials
tour.description: init.py seeds the database with initial users, menu items, and discount codes when the app boots for the first time. It is also the first intentional vulnerability in the tour: credentials are hardcoded in the seed script, making them trivially discoverable by anyone who reads the source. For ethical hackers this is the starting foothold — the credentials provide the low-privileged account from which the CTF escalation path begins.

tour.title: The Game Controller
tour.description: game.py is the developer-training layer sitting alongside the production app. It orchestrates test execution and tracks level progression, allowing a developer to run individual vulnerability tests and receive feedback on whether a fix is correct. This file is what turns a vulnerable API into an interactive game: each level corresponds to a specific vulnerability class, and passing all levels means the codebase has been hardened.

tour.title: Central API Router
tour.description: router.py is the single aggregation point for all domain routers: auth, menu, orders, admin, and referrals are each registered here and then mounted onto the app in init_app.py. Adding a new API domain requires only a new sub-router and a single line here. This file is the map of every HTTP endpoint the application exposes — reading it gives an instant inventory of the attack surface.

tour.title: Authentication: JWT & Utilities
tour.description: jwt_auth.py (fanIn=5) provides the `get_current_user` FastAPI dependency used by every protected route: it decodes the bearer token and resolves the user from the database. utils.py backs it with the primitives — password hashing, user lookup by username, and token generation. Together these two files define the authentication contract: a token issued at login is the credential that all downstream RBAC checks depend on.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI dependencies compose hierarchically: `get_current_user` itself calls `get_db` internally, so a route that declares `Depends(get_current_user)` automatically gets a database session without declaring it separately. JWT tokens are stateless — the server does not store sessions, so token revocation requires either short expiry or a separate blocklist.

tour.title: Auth Endpoints & IDOR Vulnerability
tour.description: The auth service router (app/apis/auth/service.py) exposes registration, login, profile fetch, and profile update. The profile update path delegates to patch_profile_service.py, which contains the first named vulnerability: an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) — any authenticated user can update another user's profile simply by supplying a different username in the request body, because the handler never checks that the requesting user owns the target profile.

tour.title: Orders: SQL Injection & SSRF
tour.description: The orders router handles order creation, retrieval, status checking, and delivery. It contains two vulnerabilities at depth 4 in the BFS. get_order_status.py constructs a raw SQL query by string interpolation — a classic SQL injection allowing an attacker to dump the entire database. orders/utils.py issues an HTTP request to an external URL taken verbatim from user input, a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) that can be used to probe internal services or cloud metadata endpoints.
tour.languageLesson: SQLAlchemy's ORM and `text()` with bound parameters both prevent SQL injection by separating query structure from data. Never use f-strings or `%` formatting to build SQL queries. For SSRF, the fix is an allowlist of permitted URL schemes and hostnames — rejecting requests to `169.254.169.254` (AWS metadata) and `localhost` covers the most critical cases.

tour.title: Menu: Broken Function-Level Authorization
tour.description: The menu router exposes item listing, creation, update, and deletion. delete_menu_item_service.py demonstrates a Broken Function Level Authorization (BFLA) flaw: the delete endpoint checks only that the caller is authenticated, not that they hold an admin role. Any regular user can therefore delete menu items — a privilege that should be restricted to admins according to the UserRole enum defined in models.py. This pattern of 'authenticated but not authorized' recurs across the codebase.

tour.title: Admin & Command Injection (RCE)
tour.description: The admin router serves disk usage statistics and a chef password-reset endpoint, gated behind admin authentication. admin/utils.py passes user-supplied parameters directly to a subprocess call without sanitization — a command injection vulnerability that leads to Remote Code Execution (RCE). This is the highest-severity vulnerability in the game and the final level of the CTF escalation path: an attacker who has escalated to admin can run arbitrary OS commands on the server.
tour.languageLesson: Python's `subprocess.run` with `shell=True` and unsanitized input is the canonical command injection pattern. The fix is to pass arguments as a list (shell=False) or use `shlex.quote` on any user-supplied strings. Never construct shell command strings by concatenation.

tour.title: Privilege Escalation: BFLA in User Roles
tour.description: update_user_role_service.py exposes the critical missing link in the CTF escalation chain: any authenticated user can promote themselves or another user to admin without any privilege check. Combined with the hardcoded credentials from init.py, this is the intended path — register or log in with the seeded credentials, call the role-update endpoint to become admin, then exploit the command injection in the admin service. This is the single escalation path the README describes.

tour.title: Test Suite & Vuln Proof Tests
tour.description: conftest.py sets up an in-memory test database and provides role-specific HTTP clients (anonymous, regular user, admin) that each vulnerability test uses. The level tests demonstrate what a 'proof of vulnerability' looks like: level_0 shows that the server response header leaks framework details (a disclosure vulnerability), while level_5 sends a crafted payload to the admin disk-stats endpoint and asserts that arbitrary command output is returned. Passing these tests after applying a fix is how the developer game registers progress.
tour.languageLesson: pytest's conftest.py is automatically discovered and shared across all test files in the same directory tree. Fixtures defined there (like `admin_client`) are injected by name into any test function that declares them as parameters — no import needed. The `TestClient` from Starlette wraps the ASGI app and lets tests make real HTTP calls without spinning up a server.

tour.title: Container & CI Pipeline
tour.description: The Dockerfile packages the application for deployment using a multi-stage build, but it also contains a deliberate privilege escalation vulnerability: the app user is granted passwordless sudo for the `find` command, enabling a container breakout. docker-compose.yml wires the FastAPI web service to a PostgreSQL database service and is the entry point for `./start_game.sh`. The GitHub Actions workflow in test.yml closes the loop by running pre-commit checks and the full Docker-based integration test suite on every push, ensuring the game environment stays reproducible.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds use multiple FROM statements: a builder stage installs dev dependencies and compiles assets, while the final stage copies only runtime artifacts, keeping the image small. Deliberately misconfigured sudoers entries (e.g., NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/find) are a real-world container hardening failure — even a non-root user can use `find -exec` to run arbitrary commands as root.
